name: m4rie
desc: Library for fast arithmetic with dense matrices over GF(2^e), 2<=e<=16
why: Fast GF(2^e) dense matrix arithmetic is real algebra underneath coding theory, but it is a library needing context to enjoy.

brief.what_it_is: M4RIE is a C library for fast arithmetic with dense matrices over finite fields GF(2^e) for 2 ≤ e ≤ 16. It supports basic matrix operations such as addition, equality testing, stacking, augmenting and sub-matrices, plus multiplication, row echelon form, inversion and triangular solving over those fields. Matrices go in as its own mzd/mzed data types, and results come back as matrices or echelon forms; it is a building block, not a standalone tool. It is part of the Sage mathematics software and depends on the companion library M4RI.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the name stems from the fact that the library relies heavily on M4RI, and it is aimed at dense linear algebra over small fields of even characteristic. The 2011 technical report frames it as improving on the state of the art for dense linear algebra over GF(2^e) with small e.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes a Karatsuba-style reduction, due to Boothby and Bradshaw, that turns multiplication over GF(p^k) into a series of multiplications over GF(p), giving O(n^log2 7) matrix multiplication. It also uses 'Newton-John tables', a caching technique inspired by Kronrod's M4RM method, to avoid repeated field multiplications, which gives fast row echelon form and inversion using PLE decomposition. The docs say large matrices should use the mzd_slice_t type and smaller ones the mzed_t type.

brief.install_notes: Download a release from the Bitbucket downloads page, or clone the git tree. Install M4RI first, since M4RIE depends heavily on it; the README's install section covers the M4RI clone path. The README says INSTALL has details. Building needs a GCC toolchain and autotools. Doxygen is optional, only for the reference manual. No accounts or runtimes are needed.
brief.standout: It is a niche but serious piece of algebra engineering: an asymptotically fast approach to Gaussian elimination over small extension fields, with a tech report describing the Newton-John table idea. It fills a gap for people who need dense linear algebra over GF(2^e) and do not want to hand-roll it.
brief.status: Quiet. The README history lists releases up to 2020/01/25, a small distribution bugfix. The bundled reference manual was generated in October 2014 and carries version 0.20111004. Nothing I fetched showed recent commits, and I could not check commit history because the Bitbucket page rendered only an empty shell.
brief.caveats: The README lists support for Linux, OpenSolaris and OS X, all with GCC; Windows is not mentioned. It is a C library with no CLI, so there is nothing to run directly. It depends on M4RI and needs autotools for source builds. The README's technical report abstract still says 2 ≤ e ≤ 10, while the main description says up to 16. Links to the Bitbucket wiki and downloads were not verified. The Bitbucket homepage did not render its README, so I relied on the raw README file. The licence is GPLv2 or later.
